explain.say: Here is a sort. Loud sounds: a hand dryer, a fire bell, a blender, fireworks. What helps: ear defenders, covering your ears, moving away, telling a grown-up. Well done! Your challenge: tell a grown-up which sound is too loud for you.

faq.q: Why do some sounds hurt my ears?
faq.a: Some people's ears and brains notice sounds more strongly. A loud sound can feel very big or even painful. That is real, and you can use tools.
asks: Why is noise so loud for me?

faq.a: They look like headphones with soft cushions. They block some sound, so loud noises feel quieter.
asks: Tell me about Ear defenders on

faq.q: When should I wear ear defenders?
faq.a: In very loud places, like fireworks, a busy hall, a hand dryer or a fire drill. Not all day, so your ears still hear everyday sounds.
asks: Can I wear them all day?

faq.q: What can I say when it is too loud?
faq.a: You can say, That is too loud for me. Can I move away, please? A grown-up you trust can help.

faq.q: Why do others not mind the noise?
faq.a: Everyone's ears are different. Some people hardly notice loud sounds, and some notice them a lot. Both are okay.
asks: Tell me about Others are fine

facts: Ear defenders reduce how loud sounds are when they reach your ears.
Sound loudness is measured in decibels.

quiz.say: A hand dryer is too loud. What can help?
quiz.why: Ear defenders make loud sounds quieter.

quiz.say: Why does the noise not bother everyone?
quiz.show: Why are others fine with the noise?
quiz.why: People hear sounds differently. Both ways are okay.

wrong.1: They are not pretending. Their ears just notice less.
wrong.2: They can hear. Their ears just notice loud sounds less.
